messages.author: 3a775dfa0a96bf95
messages.subject: Pairwise comparison grids
parts:
Has anyone figured out how to use ggplot to produce pairwise comparison grids (plot matrix), a la graphics::pairs? (cf. figure 2.7, p.39 in Murrell's R Graphics)

I think I can do this with facet_grid(i~j), but wouldn't that require me to make n^2 copies of my data? ... doesn't seem right....

Beyond the case where the pairwise comparisons are two different variables, I'm also interested in the case where they are different values of the same variable, e.g. compare the distributions on all pairs of weekdays.

Or is there some simple trick I'm missing here...?

Thanks,

          -s

messages.author: 3a775dfa0a96bf95
messages.subject: Re: Pairwise comparison grids
parts:
David,

Thanks for bringing plotmatrix to my attention -- I hadn't seen it because it isn't in the book.  Now I guess I need to read the man pages to see what else I'm missing.... :-(  I really prefer topical organization to alphabetical....

plotmatrix works really well in the basic case, but I can't get it to use additional aesthetics.  For example, how do I code 'gear' as color?  If I don't include 'gear' in the data frame, then there's no way of using it, but if I add the 'gear' column to the data frame, it automatically uses it as an additional value on the axes.  What's more, neither mapping(aes(colour=gear)) nor colour=gear works even then.... But I guess that's why it's called experimental.

I'm not sure I like the interface -- where all the columns are used to generate the matrix (cf. the colour problem above). It also doesn't generalize to the 'compare distributions' case (where x and y don't in general have the same number of observations) that I mentioned in my earlier email.

             -s
